_what: Provenance for the four Stage 0 items named in ledger row AUT-077: the artifact that produced each, the figure derived from it, and whether the vaccine manuscript states that figure.
_why: AUT-077 stands `queued` with `attempts: 0` over work that had already been run. This is the evidence for closing it, assembled so it can be checked.
⛔_what_this_is_not: Not a scientific result and not a quality judgement. It records that an analysis ran and that a document states its number. Every figure it points at is a binding PREDICTION or a sequence search, not a measurement of presentation, immunogenicity, efficacy or safety.
_method: each headline is derived from the artifact and then used as a search string against the manuscript, so an item is 'landed' only when both the artifact and the statement exist. Nothing here is typed from a document.
_cost: $0 — committed files and read-only git. No network, no predictor, no GPU.

ledger_row.what: Run the Stage 0 items: proteome-wide novelty, class II regeneration, anchor-position analysis, extended allele panel.

items.instrument_limit: MHCnuggets class II binding predictions. The manuscript itself grades class II prediction as substantially less accurate than class I, so one strong call on one allele is a weak positive, and no class II call here is evidence of presentation or of help delivered to a CD8 response.

headline_derived_from_the_artifact.anchor_convention_used: Anchors taken as P2 and the C-terminus for every length, which is the general class I rule and not an allele-specific motif. HLA-A*01:01 reads P3 as a primary anchor; rows for peptides called on it are marked and should be read with that caveat.

items.instrument_limit: a Hamming-distance search plus one anchor convention. Sequence distance is not T-cell-receptor distance, and the convention is a general class I rule rather than an allele-specific motif — see junction-anchor-convention-sensitivity.json, which measures how far the null travels across conventions.

last_change_curve.subject: Vaccine paper: four CI results written in, three of which change what the paper says

headline_derived_from_the_artifact.⚠_the_difference: The remaining panel alleles present no junction peptide at any threshold the data speaks to (ceiling 5.0). That is a negative reading, not a missing frequency: it was checked against the curve's own allele set and the two agree exactly.

items.instrument_limit: a class I HLA-A and HLA-B panel with no HLA-C and no class II allele, over allele frequencies pooled across populations whose frequencies differ by more than the figures reported. Every coverage number is therefore a partial coverage of the class I repertoire, and a predicted-presentation figure is not evidence that any patient's tumour presents anything.

⛔_what_none_of_these_four_covers: Step 1 of the manuscript's own §6.1 ordering — calibrating the acceptance threshold against experimentally validated epitopes — which is computational, needs only public data, and has NOT been run. coverage-threshold-curve.json supplies the threshold-agnostic curve, which is what the manuscript says is the honest report UNTIL that calibration exists; it is not the calibration.
Any measurement. Steps 2 to 4 of §6.1 need synthesised peptides, EMC tissue and matched donors, and no in-silico item substitutes for one of them.
A near-self search for the class II peptides. The one that exists covers the 11 class I binders only.
